title: ACE Omni SLEE IATO Candidate Authorization Profile
purpose: Describe and continuously test the current JAIN SLEE execution boundary as a candidate authorization architecture. This profile is evidence for assessment; it is not an authorization decision.

runtime.boundaryRule: SBB owns behavior. Resource Adaptor owns I/O.

oscal.relationship: OSCAL describes the authorization package and assurance topology; it does not grant runtime execution authority.

claims.statement: Experiment behavior and state transitions are owned by the SBB, while external effects are emitted through the Resource Adaptor contract.
The SBB does not directly import common network-client APIs and its effectful path calls the Resource Adaptor interface.
Events from another run or activity cannot mutate the active SBB state machine.
Accepted event identities are idempotent and duplicate delivery cannot produce a second command or transition.
COMPLETED and FAILED are terminal and later events cannot reopen authoritative run state.
The SLEE port and OSCAL authorization-package graph remain separate authority domains: runtime commands flow through the RA boundary, while OSCAL artifacts describe assurance and assessment evidence.

authorizationGaps.statement: No concrete deployable micro-JAIN-SLEE Resource Adaptor lifecycle and descriptor is bound in this repository.
The production deployment boundary, network paths, identities, secrets, and least-privilege service accounts are not defined by this conformance port.
Security logging, audit retention, evidence persistence, and operator access controls are not yet bound to the SLEE runtime.
The repository does not yet provide a complete system-specific OSCAL SSP, assessment plan, assessment results, or POA&M for an ACE Omni deployment.
Software supply-chain, dependency, container, host, and runtime hardening evidence must be assessed for the concrete deployment.

decisionRule: Passing this profile means the repository preserves the candidate architectural invariants. It must never be interpreted as an IATO, ATO, control pass, or authorizing-official decision.
